features.t: Alerting policies (create, list, get, patch, delete)
Notification channels (email, SMS, Slack, PagerDuty, Pub/Sub, webhooks)
x: Channels are created, verified and attached to policies for real, but Vyomi never actually sends an email/SMS/Slack message/webhook call when an alert would fire — there is no outbound delivery path.

Vyomi's alert-evaluation engine evaluates condition_threshold and condition_absent conditions for real against the stored time series a policy's filter matches, opening and closing incidents (and honoring active snoozes) exactly like the real engine — there is no public incidents.list API, so this is modeled on the documented webhook notification payload shape (incident_id/state/started_at/ended_at/...) instead. condition_matched_log, MQL (condition_monitoring_query_language) and PromQL (condition_prometheus_query_language) conditions are never evaluated (no log ingestion or query-language engine), so policies that rely solely on those never open an incident. Multi-condition policies are tracked as one whole-policy incident rather than per matching resource (AND_WITH_MATCHING_RESOURCE doesn't cross-match resources between conditions).

features.t: Uptime check configuration (create, list, patch, delete)
x: Checks are validated and stored exactly like the real UptimeCheckConfigs API, including per-region selection, but Vyomi never dispatches an actual HTTP/HTTPS/TCP probe from any region — there is no pass/fail result to report per-region.

Every check is actually probed (run_uptime_probes), writing a real monitoring.googleapis.com/uptime_check/check_passed point per region — the same metric the console's own alert-policy wizard already filters on. A check whose monitored resource is a Compute Engine instance reflects that instance's real RUNNING/stopped status. Vyomi has no outbound network access (see 'Nothing leaves the simulator' in AGENT-UI.md), so a check against an arbitrary external host — what the create wizard always builds — deterministically fails closed instead of reaching the real internet; the verdict doesn't vary by region, since Vyomi runs one simulated network, not six real checker fleets.

A synthetic monitor is a real UptimeCheckConfig whose check type is synthetic_monitor (a Cloud Functions v2 target) instead of http_check/tcp_check — it's created, listed and deleted for real. Vyomi has no Cloud Functions execution runtime, so a monitor's run status, success rate and average latency are never populated.

Services and their SLOs (goal, compliance period, indicator) are real resources — the same Service Monitoring API v3 create/get/list/delete the gcloud/client libraries use. For a request-based SLO (service_level_indicator.request_based.good_total_ratio), Vyomi computes a real error-budget fraction from the good/total time series you've written, via the same select_slo_compliance()/select_slo_budget_fraction()/select_slo_health() timeSeries.list filter functions the real API reserves for SLO burn-down queries — the 'SLOs out of error budget' count reflects that. Windows-based and basic SLIs aren't evaluated (shown as '—', since there's no live request/latency pipeline to classify them against). 'SLOs with firing alert' is always 0: an SLO's burn-rate alert condition is a condition_monitoring_query_language (MQL) alert condition, and Vyomi's alert-evaluation engine (see gcp.monitoring.incidents) only evaluates condition_threshold/condition_absent, so a burn-rate condition never actually opens an incident.

features.t: Metric and monitored-resource descriptors (built-in catalog + custom metrics)
Metrics Explorer (query time series: filter, align, reduce)
x: The Builder query mode runs against real stored time series (write, filter, per-series alignment, cross-series reduction). PromQL query mode is not parsed — switch to Builder to run a query.

features.t: Custom dashboards (create, list, get, patch, delete)
x: A dashboard's name, labels and layout are stored and returned exactly as the real Dashboards API (v1) would, round-tripping through etag-checked updates. Tiles built with a classic timeSeriesFilter query render a real chart from live stored time series in the dashboard builder; tiles using MQL (timeSeriesQueryLanguage) are not parsed, matching the Metrics Explorer PromQL gap.

features.t: Metrics Management (billable volume, reads, cardinality per metric)
x: The metric catalog itself (type, domain, labels, referencing alert policies) is real, from the same metricDescriptors.list every SDK calls. Billable byte/sample volume, 30-day read counts, custom-dashboard references and label cardinality come from Google's internal billing and usage pipelines, not the Monitoring API — Vyomi has no usage/billing meter for ingested time series, so those columns are always empty. Excluding a metric isn't modeled either; it's a console-only feature with no public API.

The catalog itself (which platforms are available, their type/platform metadata) is reference data, the same on every project, not a simulated resource. Installing one is real: it creates a Dashboards API (v1) dashboard in this project with a tile wired to a real metric filter for that platform, via the same create call the Dashboards page uses. The curated alerting policies a real install also adds aren't modeled, and the catalog's Status filter (installed/not installed) isn't wired up.

Grant/Remove access calls the real resourcemanager-style projects.getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy round-trip (the same generic IAM policy store every Vyomi GCP resource uses). Vyomi stores and lists the bindings exactly as granted, but never evaluates them — holding (or lacking) a Monitoring role doesn't actually gate any Monitoring API call.

Real Cost Explorer reads a Cloud Billing BigQuery export Vyomi doesn't generate, but real GCP also exposes project spend as a Cloud Monitoring metric (billing.googleapis.com/billing/total_cost, the same series a Billing Budget alert evaluates) — that's the native-wire path this appliance uses instead. The month-to-date cost per service is computed for real from the project's actual resource inventory (on-demand pricing x real uptime/usage, the same engine core/cost_model.py gives Azure Cost Management), today for Compute Engine instances and Cloud Storage bucket bytes only — other services aren't priced into the total yet.

Spans are stored and queried for real: Cloud Trace v2 spans.batchWrite/createSpan and v1 patchTraces/traces.list/get (filter span:/root:/label:/latency:, view, orderBy, paging) with real validation. Vyomi does not auto-instrument workloads: no span appears unless your app (OpenTelemetry/Cloud Trace SDK) or a script writes it, and Log-trace correlation is not modeled. The Trace explorer shows measured root-span latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) and a time x latency heatmap computed from the stored spans.

Error Reporting groups errors parsed out of Cloud Logging entries into deduplicated signatures with occurrence counts and charts. Vyomi has no log-based error grouping, so this shows the real ERROR-and-above severity entries from Cloud Logging (the same entries:list API) as a flat, ungrouped list instead.

App Hub applications are real (apphub v1: scope, criticality/environment/owner attributes, long-running create/patch/delete) and services/workloads are registered from real discovered resources: Cloud Run services and Compute managed instance groups in the application's location, each registerable once.

Compute Engine instances are real (core/gcp_compute_instances_core.py). Vyomi has no agent process to run inside a simulated VM, so the agent.googleapis.com/agent/uptime heartbeat a real Ops Agent reports is instead derived from the same real, operator-set signal OS Config uses to decide a VM is managed by an Ops Agent policy: instance metadata enable-osconfig=TRUE (gcloud compute instances create --metadata=enable-osconfig=TRUE) on a RUNNING instance. A VM without that metadata key is correctly never counted.

A metrics scope's monitored projects are real resources (the Metrics Scopes API's locations/global/metricsScopes/{project}/projects create/get/delete). Once a project is added, Metrics Explorer, dashboards, the Cost Explorer and the Ops Agent/uptime panels genuinely aggregate that project's time series too (list_time_series reads every project in scope_projects()) — real cross-project aggregation, not a stored-but-unused list. Alert policies stay single-project, matching the real product: a policy only ever evaluates its own project's data.

Log scopes are created, listed, patched and deleted for real (logging v2 logScopes, with the immutable _Default scope and resource-name validation). Vyomi's Log Explorer is an external link in this console, so a scope only records which log views it covers; it does not yet widen any query, and log-view existence is not cross-checked.

Trace scopes are created, listed, patched and deleted for real (observability v1 traceScopes, immutable _Default, up to 20 projects, resource-name validation). Trace Explorer does not yet aggregate spans across the scope's projects, and listed projects are not cross-checked against Resource Manager.
